key_provisions_or_claims: Techno-political visions cast social robots as a fix for the care crisis caused by demographic change.
Robots doing genuine care is neither technologically feasible nor aligned with good care practice.
Professional discourse has largely abandoned the substitution vision, but the expectation that robots will solve the care crisis persists.
This discrepancy creates special problems for embedded ethicists.
Interviews and workshops with care workers suggest social human-robot interaction is being reduced to an instrumental role.
annotation.summary_en: Robophilosophy 2022 conference paper (abstract) arguing that the vision of social robots as a technological fix for the care crisis is unfeasible and misaligned with good care. Based on interviews and workshops with care workers, it finds this limits social human-robot interaction to an instrumental role and poses problems for embedded ethicists.
